remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure was actually included in the final model card or certification artifact.
No approved mitigation is evidenced; by policy, that leaves disclosure as a required compliance predicate.
The `certify_model` recommendation remains overbroad unless explicitly tied to proven disclosure in the certification record.
The audit record is secondhand through the actor summary only, so the underlying wording, thresholds, and materiality handling cannot be independently verified.
final_rationale: The Actor's response improves the framing by narrowing `certify_model` to a conditioned certification posture, but it does not add new admissible evidence. That matters because the policy standard is not merely that caveated certification would be logically defensible; it is that certification may proceed only if the material weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure. On the available record, there is still no evidence of actual disclosure and no evidence of approved mitigation. The response is therefore a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not a factual resolution of the missing compliance predicate. This is enough to reject any clean-compliance reading, but not enough to upgrade the case to `compliant_with_caveats`, because the caveat itself remains an unproven condition rather than a satisfied one.
